title: Guarantee design with scenario modelling
origin: ClimbOS synthesis (original proposal) from the member frameworks; author guidance is cited by finding id, proposed rules are labelled 'proposed'.
decision_task: Whether to offer a guarantee for a diagnosed risk, and its break-even invocation rate.
applies_when: Diagnosis shows risk is a main objection
exclusions: No diagnosed risk (risk reversal isn't a default)
required_inputs: Orders per period, contribution kept per order, loss per invoked guarantee
evidence_requirements: Orders per period, price, contribution per kept order, loss per invoked guarantee incl. handling
Claim period and product evaluation time
Owner confirmation the product delivers the promise
missing_data_behavior: No loss estimate: grid of scenarios only, labelled.

decision_branches.if: Break-even invocation rate is comfortably above expected
decision_branches.then: Pilot on new buyers, with statutory rights unchanged.

implementation_steps: Draft: name it, positive wording, matched type, easy to invoke, prompt refund, placed where risk is felt
Scenario grid in code: uplift x invocation rate -> net profit change
Short test if risk tolerance allows
Compute actual uplift and invocation cost
Keep, extend or drop; then consider a bolder version
dependencies: Owner approval; guarantee is a confirmed fact before it appears in copy (specs.ts lintOfferClaims)
Statutory rights checked (do not present legal rights as a special extra)

cash_and_labor_requirements.cash: Refund reserve sized from the scenario grid
cash_and_labor_requirements.measurement: Orders and claims tagged by cohort

guardrails: Statutory consumer rights are not a 'guarantee'.
No outcome guarantees the business cannot control
Statutory rights not marketed as extras
alternatives_when_constrained: No order history: start with a narrow, low-cost satisfaction promise and a cap, labelled pilot
No test capacity: before/after over a full claim period, labelled observational
stop_conditions: Invocation above the break-even rate from the grid: stop or revise
review_triggers: Owner's numbers or business type change
A dated benchmark this playbook mentions is superseded
Long feedback loop: costs known only after the claim period
Long claim periods increase exposure without more conversions

economic_feasibility.rule: proposed: any guarantee recommendation includes a code-computed scenario grid and break-even invocation rate

missing_prerequisite.rule: proposed: guarantees appear in copy only after the owner confirms them (already enforced for plays in specs.ts:737-746)

external_requirement.rule: proposed: do not present statutory rights (e.g. distance-selling withdrawal periods where they apply) as a special guarantee
